questions.q: What makes a side effect different from a variable inside a program?
options: Side effects are slower
A side effect changes something outside the program, and stopping the program doesn't undo it
Side effects can only happen once
Variables are stored on disk
questions.why: Variables vanish when the program stops; the bank's record of a charge doesn't. That mismatch, fragile knowledge vs. permanent consequences, is the root problem.

questions.q: A checkout crashes after charging the card. Someone reruns it from the start. What happens?
options: It resumes and ships
It refuses to run
It reserves and charges again, then ships: the customer pays twice
Nothing, because the order already exists
questions.why: Plain code has no memory between runs, so the rerun repeats every step that already happened.

questions.q: Your program sends a charge request and gets a timeout. What do you know?
options: The customer was not charged
The customer was charged
Nothing for certain: the request or the response could have been lost
The bank is down
questions.why: This is an ambiguous failure. A timeout after sending tells you that you didn't hear back, not whether the other side acted.

questions.q: Which kind of failure is always safe to retry?
options: A timeout after the request was sent
A connection refused / 503 before the request was processed
A declined card
All of them, with enough backoff
questions.why: If the request never reached the other side, nothing happened, so retrying is safe. Timeouts are ambiguous; declines are permanent.

questions.q: Why do retries need backoff (waiting longer after each failure)?
options: To save money on API calls
So that many callers don't flood a struggling service all at once
Because servers reject retries that come too quickly
To make the code deterministic
questions.why: Without backoff, every caller retries immediately and together, and the flood (a retry storm) can keep a recovering service down.

questions.q: A customer support engineer sees 'charge failed: timeout' in a customer's logs. What should they do before telling the customer whether the card was charged?
options: Trust the log: it failed
Check the system of record (e.g., the payment provider's dashboard)
Ask the customer to retry
Restart the workflow
questions.why: Errors after a request are ambiguous. The system of record is the ground truth.
